the error message:
<simpleError: invalid version specification 1.1.3NA>

numbers in the PACKAGES file on the repository server, but not sure.

with all packages. Can you install individual packages from the
braju.com server by:

source("http://www.braju.com/R/hbLite.R");
hbLite("R.filesets");
library("R.filesets");

hbLite("aroma.core");
library("aroma.core");

Q2) Does this work?

hbLite("aroma.affymetrix");
library("aroma.affymetrix");

Q3) Does this work?

Mark (Robinson), you mentioned this problem a few weeks ago. Can you
help me troubleshoot this one?

/Henrik

CRAN/BioC packages, which is why you would expect an error if you
remove required CRAN packages such as digest. Those hbLite() commands
were only intended for troubleshooting Michael's setup.

the error, which packages managed to get installed, e.g. can you do
library("aroma.core") or library("R.filesets"), but not
library("aroma.affymetrix")?

The original error reported occurs when calling
hbInstall("aroma.affymetrix") [and I remember you mentioned the same
problem a while ago on some OSX setup]. What is really strange is
there error:
<simpleError: invalid version specification 1.1.3NA>

It looks like it there are two versions reported; first "1.1.3" then
"NA". So I guess that the package is "listed" twice "somewhere".
Mark, if you remove, say, aroma.affymetrix and aroma.core, and call
hbInstall("aroma.affymetrix"), do you get the same error?

/Henrik

want to explore too much today. However, I recall that:

server (but, since it was already installed, it didn't complain at the
end and was able to finish the installation).

Hope this helps; and thanks for the work.

Michael.

the 2.9.0 is the latest 64 bit compatible binary.

Reason for insisting on 64 bit is the large number of memory problems
during probe level/fragment length normalization, which require
frequent process restarts (with R restart after Rcache deletion),
sometimes already after ca. 20 x 6.0 arrays (though my series are
frequently > 100). I am hoping that the memory management under 64 bit
may help here (the processes themselves are not that big; the max I
have seen went into 2.5GB).

There is a problem with the source option, too; hope, this is easily
found ;-)

Best,

Michael.
